newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 2.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Rugby League announced yesterday Coca-Cola will sponsor the State of Origin series for the next three years in a deal reportedly around A$1.5 million to A$2 million. The sponsorship is a coup for the ARL, as Super League still has no namin sponsor for its equivalent competition, the Tri-Series. Page 24.

West Australian cyclist Henk Vogels is on a mission to win the Paris-Roubaix classic, known as cycling's most punishing and prestigious one-day race, after finishing 10th in the event last year, the best placing by an Australian. Page 22.

Townsville Suns basketball team coach Mark Bragg steered the team into the NBL in 1993 and has seen it progress well, with it attracting 55 consecutive capacity crowds (4141) and enjoying being one of only two profitable clubs in the League. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

National soccer coach Terry Venables yesterday announced a 33-man squad for the Superstars series next month, a two match, made-for-television series that will effectively be a final World Cup selection trial. Of the 33 players named, only 22 will be selcted for the opening round of World Cup qualifiers against Tahiti and the Solomon Islands. Page 42.

While a press conference involving Sydney Swans captain Paul Kelly, and Carlton's Ang Christou and Matthew Allan at the Sydney Harbour Casino yesterday was designed to be a promotional plug for the Sydney/Carlton match this weekend, it ended up becoming a quasi debate about the race issue infecting the AFL. Page 42.

The New South Wales rugby team is in Napier glad to escape a barrage of criticism over their loss last weekend to the ACT Brumbies. The Waratahs face Wellington in a must-win match in the Super 12 competition, and will be boosted by the return of internationals David Campese, Phil Kearns, and Michael Brial. Page 42.
THE AGE

Hawthorn's Brendan Krummel does not look likely to take the field in the AFL match against North Melbourne tomorrow night after being poked in the eye in the match against Sydney last Saturday. Sydney's Jason Mooney has been asked to front the AFL Tribunal on Monday night in relation to the incident. Page D3.

In a move sure to please the purists, Australia's grand slam tennis event will be known simply as the Australian Open for the first time in 25 years. Ford will continue its sponsorship of the event, but no longer has naming rights. Page D10.

Rachel Imison, 18, yesterday played her first hockey game in goals for the Australian Hockeyroos in a match against the Australian senior youth. However, her match does not count as an international debut, but if she is picked to play against New Zealandor China, two other participants in the current four-team tournament, she will get her first international cap. Page D13.
THE HERALD SUN

The Essendon AFL club will meet with the AFL today over the Dean Wallis affair. Wallis was cited for charging Collingwood's Andrew Schauble, yet field umpire John Harvey initially did not make a report after viewing the video. Essendon claims Harvey was instructed to report Wallis even though he had decided there was no charge. Page 104.

Australian women's basketballer Robyn Maher will tomorrow play her 300th WNBL game against Melbourne, and is only the third player to do so. Maher has little left to achieve in her career, having competed in three Olympics, five world championships, and inning the Most Valuable Player award twice. Page 90.

The West Coast Eagles AFL team will recall champion centre half-back Glen Jakovich, almost a year since he underwent knee construction surgery for a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament. Jakovich will join the team for tomorrow night's match against the Wstern Bulldogs at the WACA. Page 101.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Balmain rugby league player Tim Brasher was yesterday convicted of assault following a dispute with a student on the North Ryde Golf Course on February 9. The Ryde Local Court heard Brasher grabbed the student by the neck when he became impatient with the time the student was taking to play. Page 116.

New Zealand-trained racehorse Vialli has suffered a cracked hoof, bashed his coronet, pulled a muscle, and has been sick with infections and viruses, but, thanks to his class, he will be making his Queensland debut in the weight-for-age Hart Stakes (1400 etres) at Eagle Farm tomorrow. Page 110.

Sydney long-distance swimmer Susie Maroney left Australia for the United States yesterday, saying she was not making her second attempt at the Cuba to the United States swim to defy critics, but was doing it for her own personal satisfaction. Her second attempt is planned to begin on May 8. Page 112.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
